overview: Reverse Logistics Grading and Recovery addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in logistics and supply chain operations. The first proof of value uses returned product inspections, resale values and warranty terms. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is net recovered value per return, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: returned product inspections, resale values and warranty terms; define net recovered value per return and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Logistics COO / Supply Chain Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
